approaches.title: Full seat-matrix simulation
approaches.summary: Allocates a boolean seat array for every cinema row, marks reservations, and greedily checks the three possible family blocks in each row. This version is marked wrong and can run out of memory for large n.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Initial implementation using a full n-by-10 seat matrix and greedy placement of family blocks, with debug output. It is marked wrong due to OOM.

approaches.title: Sort and process reserved rows
approaches.summary: Sorts reservations by row, groups reservations belonging to the same row, and processes each group with a local ten-seat boolean array. Unreserved rows contribute two families directly.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces the full seat matrix with sorted row groups, tracking only rows containing reservations and adding two families for each untouched row.

revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 1386: bit masks & unnecessary secondary sorting
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Keeps the sorted/grouped strategy but represents reserved seats with bitmasks and evaluates the three family intervals using bit operations.

approaches.title: HashMap of reserved-row bitmasks
approaches.summary: Builds a hash map from row numbers to reserved-seat bitmasks without sorting the reservations. It counts two families for rows with no relevant reservations and evaluates each affected row with interval masks.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Changes from sorting and contiguous grouping to a HashMap that aggregates reservation masks by row, while retaining bitmask-based interval checks.

revisions.commitComment: range limit already causes hashmap to only contain single 4 seat
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 1386: range limit already causes hashmap to only contain single 4 seat
revisions.commitBody:
- range limit guarantees that if the entry exists either ends of the row
is not free. Meaning, only 1 family of 4 can seat.

- since it's only ever +1, we can just use a simple iterator to filter
and count
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Simplifies affected-row handling: because only seats 2 through 9 create map entries, each affected row contributes at most one family. Counts rows with any available family interval instead of branching over the three cases.
